posts.title: Shakira Sets Amazon Music Livestream Record With Madrid Show and Dua Lipa Duet
posts.excerpt: Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert became Amazon Music's most-viewed livestream by a female artist, with Dua Lipa joining her for a surprise performance of "Antología."
posts.body:
Shakira's October 3 Madrid concert became Amazon Music's most-viewed livestream by a female artist, with Dua Lipa joining her for a surprise performance of "Antología." Amazon announced the record the following day but did not publish a viewer total.

The show streamed worldwide through Amazon Music, Prime Video and Twitch and marked Shakira's first full-concert global livestream. Amazon's record claim applies specifically to its own platform, not to concert streams across every service. The broadcast was also part of Amazon Music's 2026 Women Shaping Latin Music campaign.

The concert took place at Shakira Stadium, the temporary venue built inside Madrid's Iberdrola Music complex for the residency. "Antología" comes from *Pies Descalzos*, released in 1995. Dua had already covered the song at her own Bogotá show in 2025 while Shakira was performing it the same night in Asunción. Madrid was the first time the two sang it together onstage.

[ig:p:DeFRhLolil0|@shakira|https://www.instagram.com/p/DeFRhLolil0/]

The Madrid residency is part of Es Latina, a month-long cultural program built around Macondo Park. The temporary site surrounds the stadium with themed spaces devoted to music, literature, fashion, food and other parts of Latin culture. It includes a Shakira museum, a literature area inspired by Gabriel García Márquez and additional performances around the main concerts. The October 3 livestream captured one night inside that larger temporary project.

posts.title: Frequency Of Love
posts.excerpt: Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul.
posts.body:
Victoria Monét has released her second album *Frequency Of Love*, a 22-song record that moves between R&B, house, funk and acoustic soul. Released October 2, it is her first full-length since *JAGUAR II*, which won Best R&B Album as Monét took Best New Artist at the 2024 Grammys.

The gap was deliberate. Monét has said she wanted enough life to happen before making the next record, and part of that time took her to culinary school. She graduated from the Institute of Culinary Education in May 2026 and completed an externship at Verse L.A. while rehearsing for Bruno Mars' European stadium tour. Cooking gave her a way to make something without immediately turning it into promotion or income after the long Grammy cycle around *JAGUAR II*.

*Frequency Of Love* began with a narrower idea. Monét was tracing musicians who worked on records by Michael Jackson and Quincy Jones, which led her toward Toto and yacht rock. Culinary school disrupted that plan in a useful way. She matched what she was cooking with music from the same place, listening to Italian music on pasta days and Jamaican music when the class made Jamaican food. The final album keeps some of the yacht-rock influence but moves well beyond it.

"Reach Out" leans into house, "You Hurt Me Too" was written with a James Bond theme in mind, and "Juicy" keeps more of the yacht-rock idea. "Reach Out" also predates the album. Monét recorded it around the period when the *JAGUAR II* deluxe edition was being assembled, then held it back because she thought it deserved more than a bonus-track slot. Its video was shot at the Salk Institute in La Jolla.

[youtube:h99lQg2zSl0]

Monét has described love on the album broadly, including romance, heartbreak, self-love and motherhood. Her daughter Hazel Monét appears with Leon Thomas on "You Mean The World To Me," bringing that family thread directly into the record. Elsewhere, the songs move between attraction, disappointment and the risk that comes with letting someone close.

The album also reaches back to "Somebody," a mid-century standard Monét first heard as a child while watching *Introducing Dorothy Dandridge* with her grandmother. Dandridge stayed with her long enough that Monét later dressed as her for Halloween twice. The reference sits naturally beside the album's newer R&B and dance ideas without turning into a separate nostalgia exercise.

Monét takes *Frequency Of Love* on a 27-city North American tour beginning October 27 in Raleigh. She is also launching the Frequency Of Love Foundation, which plans youth programs around food, agriculture, cooking and wellness. Its first plans include hands-on food education and community gardens, keeping the culinary work that shaped this album connected to what comes after it.
